subject: renjin with java matrix data set

messages.author: 123e00362cef0fea
messages.subject: renjin with java matrix data set
parts:
Not sure if this is the right forum to post a question like this, but I could not find any other place or documentation for renjin issues

I am considering using renjin to execute R code from a java client.  The idea is to work with a matrix or a data table  (Object[][]) as an input and do R-calculations that would return a value for each row.  The result would then be a vector, like a new column that I would add to the data table.  I think this is frequently done using data frames in R.  I am a java developer with a limitied experince of R, but the users of the client like R for various calculations.

So far I have the renjin working by using the java script engine and have been testing out some very simple calculations with single values and vectors.  I have not succeeded or found out how I perform R calculation using java Object[][] as the input.  The put() method seams to accept the matrix, but I have not been able to run any eval command.  In the excample belove I am simpy trying to retrive the value of location [1,2]. I have tried various syntax without success.  Could you give me a hint or direct me to some documentation for this problem.


engine = factory.getEngineByName("Renjin");

Long[][] numbers = new Long[1000][100];

for (int row=0; row<numbers.length; row++) {

       for (int col = 0; col<numbers[row].length; col++) {

             int numb = new Random().nextInt(10000000);

             numbers[row][col] = (long)numb;

       }

}

engine.put("Matrix", numbers);  // This seams to store the data set successfully

Object ep = engine.eval("Matrix[1][2]");  // this throws invalid source exceptions

System.out.println(ep);


 

Best regards,

Ragnar

messages.author: f06db63329fab1f9
messages.subject: Re: renjin with java matrix data set
parts:
Hi Ragnar,
 
A "matrix" in R is simply a vector with a dimension ("dim") attribute. The R syntax for accessing matrix elements is Matrix[1,2].

To create a matrix from Java code, you can use the DoubleMatrixBuilder utility class:
https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/blob/master/core/src/main/java/org/renjin/primitives/matrix/DoubleMatrixBuilder.java

This will create an R matrix in memory with the appropriate dimension attribute.

You can also subclass the DoubleVector class if your matrix is strangely shaped or not stored in memory.

Best,
Alex

messages.author: f06db63329fab1f9
messages.subject: Re: renjin with java matrix data set
parts:
Column and row names for R matrices are specified in the "dimnames" attribute, which should be a ListVector containing a StringVector each dimension. In R, this looks like:

x <- c(1,2,3,4,5,6) 
attr(x, "dim") <- c(2L, 3L) # now a 2 x 3 matrix
attr(x, "dimnames") <- list( c("row 1", "row 2"), c("column 1", "column 2", "column 3") )

This will then look like this in R:
> x
      column 1 column 2 column 3
row 1        1        3        5
row 2        2        4        6

You can construct the dimnames attribute in Java using the ListVector.Builder and the StringArrayVector.Builder classes (or StringArrayVector.valueOf("row 1", "row 2") if the names are fixed)

A data.frame object in R is something else. It's basically a list of columns. In R, you could construct one by "hand" in the following way

> df <- list( c(1,2,3,4), c(10,20,30,40 ))   # Create a list of two columns
> attr(df, "names") <- c("x", "y")   # Give those columns names
> attr(df, "row.names") <- as.character(1:4) # Assign row names
> attr(df, "class") <- "data.frame"
> df
  x  y
1 1 10
2 2 20
3 3 30
4 4 40


Note again that your data doesn't have to sit in memory, you can provide your own implementation of IntVector or StringVector for your own data sources. 

What we really need is a good little library of helper functions for Java developers that would facilitate the creation of all these different types of R objects: data.frames, matrices, time series, etc, because it can be definitely a little opaque. 

HTH
Alex
